answer: Sybil resistance needs a signal that cannot be replayed. Each identity signs the epoch's random challenge and locks a 500 POA bond for 30 epochs, so a clone must post its own bond instead of borrowing one. Standing accumulates on a summit that rises only while every epoch carries a fresh signed signal; a gap resets the climb. The plume of reputation decays over 10 idle epochs, so dormant clones bleed standing together. Since each clone needs its own bond and signed history, attacker cost grows linearly per identity while rewards stay flat; peers verify each signature on-chain.
